answer: A sybil farmer's real edge is that shells are nearly free to create and cost nothing to idle, while an honest user is bounded by their own effort. Destroy that edge: make every reward claim cost fresh, unpredictable, identity-keyed useful work. Each epoch the network issues verification tasks bound to the claimant's public key, so one computation can never serve two shells. Like tending a meadow, the tide of required work rises daily, and any identity at its nadir of contribution earns nothing. A farm of a thousand shells must do a thousand times the real work, erasing the clone's free ride.
